headline: Europe's bio-based and forest materials sector is in a cost-squeezed, restructuring phase: incumbents are cancelling textile-fibre projects and moving into packaging, while EU policy and Horizon calls keep supporting the bioeconomy.
outlook_reason: Policy and funding are supportive, but weak pulp and fibre markets, cost inflation and the cancelled Metsä Kuura textile mill limit near-term demand for new materials.

signals.title: Metsä Group Q3 2026 results
signals.detail: Q3 comparable EBITDA EUR 100 million versus 39 million a year earlier. Softwood pulp demand is expected to stay subdued. Paperboard balance has improved. Kemi mill has a longer Q4 maintenance shutdown.

signals.title: Kemira Q1–Q3 2026 report
signals.detail: Q3 revenue EUR 708.9 million (+3 %), flat excluding acquisitions. Profitability is burdened by raw-material inflation of about EUR 100 million. FY2026 operative EBITDA guidance is EUR 400–500 million. Citrawasserchemie acquisition completed.

signals.title: Horizon Europe bridging calls open
signals.detail: HORIZON-BRIDGING-2027-02-05 has EUR 32.5 million for about 13 grants. It funds follow-on innovation from completed Pillar II projects, with a maximum of 6 partners. Deadline 2027-01-28.

signals.title: Spinnova files SEC registration for US IPO
signals.detail: Spinnova plans a Nasdaq Capital Market dual listing raising at least USD 15 million, against a market cap of about EUR 27 million. The offering was expected in Sep–Oct 2026. I found no confirmation that it was completed.

signals.title: Metsä invests EUR 25 million in Muoto and cancels Kuura textile mill
signals.detail: Commercial Muoto fibre-packaging line at Äänekoski from 2028 (Valmet supplier). Kuura textile fibre mill in Kemi cancelled because of Asian overcapacity and weak premium for responsible fibres.
